correctness.rationale: For every finite connected H with nonadjacent twin pair of degree d, both endpoint rows share the same neighbor sum. This gives exact antisymmetric eigenvalue rho=1/(d+1) whenever only uv is inactive. Stochastic sup-norm nonexpansion bounds perturbations and keeps every H-edge receptive. The confidence/gap ratio D rho^t/(c delta^t) yields both phases with strict equality handled. After activation the antisymmetric base cancels completely in P_G and the perturbation is within epsilon of consensus; c_uv becomes at least gamma, so full receptivity persists and primitive connected stochastic averaging converges. At the critical equality uv never activates. The code independently checked the actual model by exact fractions with 56,706 executed assertions across 140 graphs, five rates each, and critical special cases. Finite tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The initiating source develops this exact model and establishes eventual confidence and effective-graph convergence, while explicitly suggesting further analysis of edges between same-limit opinion pairs. The present statement derives a new exact graph-local and parameter-sharp cutoff, an explicit first restoration time, a critical waiting-time divergence, and a stable open set of initial conditions across all connected twin-containing graphs. Actual semantic research-record and targeted literature queries found no covering proposition. This is a best-knowledge originality assessment, not a proof of publication priority.

value.rationale: Li, Luo and Porter identify consensual but mutually unreceptive agents in the adaptive-confidence HK model and explicitly identify parameter-dependent edge retention as future work. The theorem gives a structural explanation valid across connected networks with a common-neighbor twin pair, not a single contrived numerical run: a sharp topology-local critical forgetting rate, robust open initial conditions, finite first trust-restoration time, and inverse-distance critical slowing. It distinguishes two limiting effective networks while all opinions converge to consensus. This is a motivated precise boundary theorem rather than a generic model simulation or a mere restatement of a convergence lemma.
